preamble: The source here is vocalic (syllabic) r̩, which has no separate atlas symbol and is filed under r, just as l_to_u files syllabic l̩. In Middle Indo-Aryan the Old Indo-Aryan vowel ṛ [r̩] was lost and replaced by a plain vowel: Pali and the Prakrits show a, i or u. The u outcome is conditioned: it appears when the following syllable contains u (Sanskrit ṛtu > Pali utu, ṛju > uju) or next to a labial consonant (pṛcchati > pucchati, vṛddha > vuḍḍha, spṛṣṭa > phuṭṭha), while elsewhere ṛ usually gives a or i (kṛta > kata, ṛṣi > isi). The conditioning is a tendency, not absolute: vṛkṣa 'tree' gives Pali rukkha, not vukkha.
